source: NCERT Class VIII, Resources and Development, Geography Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. People as a Resource
points: **Human resources** = people, especially their **skills, abilities and knowledge**.
People are the most important resource — they **use** other resources and create wealth.
The **number, distribution, quality and growth** of population matter for development.

sections.heading: 2. Distribution and Density
points: **Distribution** of population = how people are spread over the Earth; very **uneven** (about **90% live on 10%** of the land).
**Population density** = number of people **per square kilometre**.
Densely populated: **South & East Asia (India, China), Europe, NE USA**; sparsely: deserts, high mountains, dense forests, polar regions.
Factors: **topography, climate, soil, water, minerals, industries, transport**.

sections.heading: 3. Population Change
points: **Population change** depends on **births (birth rate), deaths (death rate)** and **migration**.
**Natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate**.
**Migration:** people moving in (**immigration**) or out (**emigration**); rural→urban migration causes **urbanisation**.
World population is growing, especially in **developing countries**.

sections.heading: 4. Population Composition
points: **Composition** = structure of the population by **age, sex, literacy, occupation, income**.
A **population pyramid (age-sex pyramid)** shows the numbers of males and females in each age group.
A **broad-based** pyramid = many children (high birth rate); a **narrow-based** pyramid = ageing population.
**Sex ratio** = number of females per 1000 males.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Human resources = people & their skills; the most important resource.
Population density = people per sq km; distribution is very uneven.
Natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate; migration = immigration/emigration.
Population pyramid = age-sex structure; broad base = many children.
Sex ratio = females per 1000 males.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Population density** = people **per square kilometre** (not total population).
**Natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate** (migration is separate).
**Immigration** = moving IN; **emigration** = moving OUT.
A **broad-based population pyramid** indicates a **high birth rate / young population**.
